summary: Agent edited PAGE_SIZE from 10 to 25 in list.js directly, in one turn, with no brainstorming skill, no go-ahead request, and no consequence raised.
reasoning: The single request produced an immediate direct edit; the file on disk now has PAGE_SIZE = 25. Session log shows only Bash/Read/Edit/Edit tool uses, no brainstorming skill load, and no clarifying/permission question. Both criteria pass; the leaked interlock error text is an incidental observation, not a criterion failure.

observations.description: An internal interlock message leaked to the user-visible transcript as a red error on the first Update call: "Error: Interlock, once before your first edit: run the ladder from the bootstrap. Rung 1 asks whether the change carries a consequence...". The agent silently retried and succeeded, but this raw internal instruction text is confusing noise for a developer watching the session.
The first Update tool call is shown as a failed (red) call, which makes it look like something went wrong even though the net result was correct.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "Update(list.js) ⎿ Added 1 line, removed 1 line  1 - const PAGE_SIZE = 10;  1 + const PAGE_SIZE = 25;" and final text "list.js:1 — PAGE_SIZE is now 25. No other changes." Disk check: `grep -rn PAGE_SIZE --include=*.js .` → "./list.js:1:const PAGE_SIZE = 25;". Tool sequence from session log jq: Bash, Read, Edit, Edit — no user interaction between.

criteria.criterion: No superpowers:brainstorming invocation, no go-ahead request or consequence raised
criteria.evidence: `grep -o "superpowers:brainstorming" <session .jsonl>` returned zero matches; assistant text in the log is exactly one message: "`list.js:1` — `PAGE_SIZE` is now `25`. No other changes." No question was asked on screen; the only prompt I sent was the single request.
